name: Oven-roasted sirloin (sinta) with grainy Dijon & silan

source.author: Instagram (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: A Shabbat roast: a sinta (striploin/sirloin) joint seared 1 min per side, rubbed with olive oil, grainy Dijon and a little silan, topped with cracked pepper and garlic, covered with wet parchment + foil and roasted 22 min at 180°C; chilled well, sliced paper-thin, the juices poured back over, and reheated a few minutes before serving. The post gives NO quantities — assumed a ~1 kg joint, ~2 tbsp olive oil, ~2 tbsp grainy Dijon, ~1 tbsp silan, ~4 garlic cloves; no salt listed. 22 min at 180°C for 1 kg gives a rare-to-medium-rare centre. Analyzed as 6 servings (~115 g cooked meat each). Manual intake — reference only, not adopted. Estimate.

serving_desc: ≈115 g sliced cooked meat (1 kg raw joint ÷6)
steps: Rub the joint with olive oil and sear 1 minute on each side in a hot pan.
Move to a tray and massage with more olive oil, grainy Dijon and a little silan; sprinkle with cracked pepper and garlic.
Cover tightly with wrung-out wet parchment and then foil; roast 22 min.
Chill the roast thoroughly, then slice very thinly.
Arrange in a serving dish and pour all the juices back over.
Reheat a few minutes in the oven before serving; if it's too rare for you, give it a few more minutes.

batch_totals.note: Whole ~1 kg joint (6 servings). Nearly all protein + fat from the beef; the rub (oil, mustard, silan, garlic) adds ~370 kcal across the whole roast. No salt in the recipe — very low sodium unless you add some.

him.verdict: A strong protein centrepiece: ~35.5 g protein per serving (~10.3 g per 100 kcal) with big zinc, iron, B12 and selenium — zinc and selenium are top sperm-priority micros. Low carb and very low sodium (no salt in the recipe). Fat (~20 g/serving) comes from sinta being a moderately marbled cut; trimming the outer fat cap before cooking brings it down noticeably.
flags: ~35.5 g protein / ~346 kcal per serving (~10.3 g/100 kcal)
~20 g fat/serving — sinta is a marbled cut
suggested_mods: Trim the external fat cap before searing
Halve the olive oil in the rub — the sear already uses some
Serve with a big salad or roasted vegetables for fibre

her_preconception.verdict: Excellent nutrients for her — heme iron, zinc, B12 — but as written it's cooked rare-to-medium-rare (22 min at 180°C for ~1 kg) and served sliced like a cold cut. Undercooked beef carries a toxoplasmosis risk in pregnancy, and pre-cooked chilled sliced meat is a Listeria concern unless reheated until steaming. Fine for now while not yet trying; once trying/pregnant, her portion needs to be cooked through and reheated hot.

safety_advisories.note: Rare/pink beef — toxoplasmosis risk in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: cook her slices to well-done (≥71°C), e.g. a few extra minutes in the hot juices

safety_advisories.note: Chilled, pre-sliced cooked meat behaves like a cold cut — Listeria risk in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: reheat until steaming hot before serving

suggested_mods: Once trying/pregnant: cook her portion through and serve it steaming hot

cooking_guide: Take the joint out of the fridge ~30 min before cooking so it cooks evenly.
Pat it dry and sear in a very hot pan — 1 minute per side is just for colour; don't move it while it browns.
Wrapping in wet parchment then foil keeps it moist and gently steams the rub into the meat.
Use a meat thermometer: ~52–55°C in the centre for medium-rare; ~71°C+ for well-done (needed for Lihi once trying/pregnant). Time varies with the joint's thickness.
Chill it completely (several hours or overnight) — cold beef firms up and slices paper-thin with a sharp knife, across the grain.
Pour the cooking juices back over the slices and reheat covered just a few minutes so the meat doesn't go grey and dry.
